title: The image of the invisible God (Colossians 1:15–20)
word: The image of the invisible God
hookLine: an early hymn: in him all things hold together
tomorrow: rooted and built up: why does Paul mix a tree and a house?

lines: A PHOTO OF SOMEONE YOU'VE NEVER MET.
THE IMAGE OF THE INVISIBLE GOD.
cards: A photo of someone you've never met still tells you things: the face, the smile, the way they hold their shoulders.
A new letter, to believers in a small town called Colosse, says something much bolder about Jesus: "Who is the image of the invisible God." A face you can look at, of someone nobody can see.
And then the lines start to swing and balance, like a song.

teach.h: A HYMN? THE LETTER DOESN'T SAY.
teach.b: Some readers think Paul is quoting a hymn the churches already sang. The letter doesn't say. Christians read the first line this way: look at Jesus, and you see what God is like.
Then the song widens as far as it can go: "For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible."

Then one short line: "And he is before all things, and by him all things consist." Consist, in the King James, means hold together. Here's one to tell a friend: the verse isn't only about a beginning.
It's about right now. Not made once and left on a shelf, but held. Then the song comes close: he is "the head of the body, the church," "the firstborn from the dead."
And it ends where this whole stretch of letters keeps ending, in peace: God is "to reconcile all things unto himself," having "made peace through the blood of his cross."
Listen to the phrase that keeps coming back: all things. Made, held, reconciled. No corner left out.

how: Colossians 1:15–20 is read and sung in Christian worship, and some churches use it as a canticle in their daily prayers.

games.q: what does “the image of the invisible god” mean?
o: a mirror that shows your soul
a painting of God hung in a church
Jesus as the visible face of an unseen God

games.q: the song in Colossians — tap the pairs.

s: Colossians pictures God making the world once and leaving it alone
by him all things consist: held together, right now.
the letter itself says these lines were a hymn
some readers think so, from how they balance; the letter doesn't say.
the passage says peace was made through the blood of his cross
to reconcile all things unto himself, having made peace.

games.q: a kid in your Sunday school class asks: 'if nobody can see God, how do Christians know what God is like?' what fits Colossians 1?
o: they look at Jesus: the image of the invisible God.
they can't know anything at all about what God is like.
they look at old paintings of God in well-known churches.
games.why: Christians read Colossians 1:15 as: look at Jesus, and you see what God is like. a sentence a parent could say at dinner.

practice: Walk slowly through one room for a minute, noticing what holds it together: a hinge, a seam, a nail, a photo of people you love. Then sit, and name the one thing, or the one person, who held your day together.

wordCard.voice: The image of the invisible God. Colossians' words for Jesus: a face you can look at, of a God nobody can see.

orig.note: Greek: image, in Colossians 1:15: something that can be looked at.

carryVoice: The line to keep: all things hold together, held right now, not just made once. Two weeks of letters, done.
